timeline.body:
Instead of conditionalizing flag AVX3Threshold on a JVMCI-versioned
JDK 11, expect it for any JDK >= 11

Closes #2402
The check will now fail on earlier JDK 11s that don't have this flag so the check needs to take the update version into account.

> The check will now fail on earlier JDK 11s that don't have this flag so the check needs to take the update version into account.

I take it `>= 11.0.6` would be OK?

> I take it `>= 11.0.6` would be OK?

This added reflectiveness makes it quite ugly. Perhaps there is some less clunky way to do this?

You should use a regular expression to parse the value of the `java.vm.version` system property. Here are some sample values:
11.0.7+8-LTS-jvmci-20.1-b02
25.241-b07-jvmci-20.1-b01

reply.body:
`UNSET` is just the default. I was trying to avoid all this version parsing mess. In particular, for this issue I'm not sure it's worth doing the right thing for JDK 8, is it? If that's needed, I'd rather have a specialized class which only deals with that and is unit-tested.

So if `Runtime.version().update()` cannot be used, how about `Runtime.Version.parse(<value>)` where `<value>` could be coming from `java.vm.version` property as you say?

So I'd be something like: http://hg.openjdk.java.net/jdk8u/jdk8u/jdk/file/e6178063e9dd/test/sun/misc/Version/Version.java#l139 for `java.vm.version` parsing for JDK 8. For JDK 9+ we really should leverage the JDK for the parsing rather than writing our own.
For 8, *only* JVMCI JDKs can be used (currently) so we can rely on JVMCI versions there.

That's what I mean. It'll fail for all sorts of weird versions. I'm pretty sure this fails for my hypothetical JDK 8 here: `java.vm.version = 25.242-b08`. Since we don't need to cover JDK 8 - covered by jvmci, why would we want to craft a custom parser which then fails in strange ways. Example for JDK 14 I have here: `java.vm.version = 14+36`.

Can there really be a lot of variation in values for the `java.version` system property? The specification for [Runtime.Version](https://download.java.net/java/GA/jdk14/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Runtime.Version.html) includes a regular expression for a _version number_ and I think `java.version` will always be a version number as opposed a more variable _version string_. In any case a version string is specified to always start with a version number.

If your really want to rely on using `Runtime.Version` for parsing `java.version` (which I'm not objecting to), then you will have to use an [overlay](https://github.com/graalvm/mx/blob/master/README.md#versioning-sources-for-different-jdk-releases) which is a larger change.

timeline.body: @dougxc I've updated it to use JDK parsing logic for JDK 11+ and a simple regex for JDK 8. Hope that seems reasonable.

> We only use reflection where absolutely necessary in Graal, especially in Graal initialization code. Can you please replace the reflection with this new method in `GraalServices`:
> 
> ```
>     /**
>      * Gets the update-release counter for the current Java runtime.
>      *
>      * @see "https://download.java.net/java/GA/jdk14/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Runtime.Version.html"
>      */
>     public static int getJavaUpdateVersion() {
>         throw shouldNotReachHere();
>     }
> ```

OK.
@dougxc Not sure if you rather wanted `Runtime.Version.parse(System.getProperty("java.vm.version")).update()` here. Let me know if so.

reply.body: No, this is exactly what we want. If `Runtime.Version.parse(System.getProperty("java.vm.version")).update() != Runtime.version().update()`, then I'd say there are bigger problems.

timeline.body: This now looks good. I'll start integrating it.
Thanks for the review and your help!

timeline.message:
Expect AVX3Threshold on all JDKs >= 11.0.6 or JDK >= 14

Instead of conditionalizing flag AVX3Threshold on a JVMCI-versioned
JDK 11, expect it for any JDK 11 >= 11.0.6

Closes #2402
